body: Can you check the results with the line changed to `ref_vec = mix(ref_vec, bent_normal, roughness * roughness * roughness * roughness);`? I just went through the source and this calculation seems to consistently use the wrong roughness mapping (it's used for sky lighting too). If I'm correct, then simply using the correct mapping should look good enough and it won't reintroduce the problem that https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/62547 fixes

> I think part of what makes the cubemap stretching so obvious because the mipmaps just don't look amazing and have some projection artifacts.

If we had support for [offline reflection probe baking](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4782), we could bake them to a 2× resolution on each axis and use VRAM compression. This way, they occupy the same space in VRAM as they do currently (since VRAM compression of HDR formats has a 1:4 compression ratio). Offline baking also makes it possible to use supersampling to reduce aliasing in the rendered reflection probe, which helps at lower roughness levels.

Bicubic sampling for reflection probes is technically feasible, but it means we wouldn't be able to use the hardware's native support for seamless cubemaps anymore. I can foresee this being quite expensive on the GPU.

There's a detail with perceptual roughness that's confusing me a lot. Looking at the Google Filament code [here](https://github.com/google/filament/blob/main/shaders/src/surface_shading_lit.fs#L49), we see that when they do specular AA, they convert the value to perceptual roughness. Godot only does this in some operations, for example [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_clustered/scene_forward_clustered.glsl#L1578) and [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_clustered/scene_forward_clustered.glsl#L1583). I'm not sure, but I believe that perceptual roughness and linear roughness isn't being applied correctly in many parts of the code, which also made me realize that my DFG LUT PR that was recently merged isn't using perceptual roughness.

One last thing: does Godot clamp the roughness? Because I haven't seen Godot do this like Google Filament does, for example [here](https://github.com/google/filament/blob/main/shaders/src/surface_shading_lit.fs#L217). Is there a reason why this isn't done?"

I'm not sure, but I believe that perceptual roughness and linear roughness isn't being applied correctly in many parts of the code, which also made me realize that my DFG LUT PR that was recently merged isn't using perceptual roughness.

Godot uses perceptual roughness and only converts into linear roughness as needed. Those lines you point out aren't converting from linear roughness to perceptual roughness. They are mapping perceptual roughness to the mapping used by the specular filtering code (which happens to also be a sqrt mapping). 

> One last thing: does Godot clamp the roughness? Because I haven't seen Godot do this like Google Filament does, for example [here](https://github.com/google/filament/blob/main/shaders/src/surface_shading_lit.fs#L217). Is there a reason why this isn't done?"

Filament needs to clamp roughness because they are using half floats. Godot uses full floats everywhere so it isn't necessary.
